doc.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007

title: Editing the single and working with engineers like Gene Paul
summary: Monk Rowe asks about razor-blade editing. Dorn says engineers do the cutting and reflects on the randomness in art.

story.theme_name: Tape changes, reel headers and session breaks
story.community_name: Tape changes, reel headers and session breaks

blocks.x: And when you edited it, did you take a razor blade to it? The master tape?
Well we never do the master tape.
I mean not the master tape, but —
Yeah, well somebody put a razor blade to it. If I would put a razor blade to anything what you would have is tape pudding.
But you took out a verse or —
I don’t even remember what it was. But I shortened it. You know, I always work with good engineers. So you know, you’ve been there when we do our magic, with Gene, I work with Gene [Paul] you know.
Yeah but I mean besides the fact that it’s a great story, does it give you a sense of like how brilliant everybody is? There’s a lot of randomness that goes into any art I think.
